summary.headline: Entero Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32.9% to INR2,087 crore; management says FY27 will beat its 23% growth guidance without quantifying it.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 32.9% YoY to INR2,087 crore in Q2 FY27, with organic growth of 18.2% and inorganic contribution of 14.7% from calendarised prior-year acquisitions. Gross margin rose 126 bps to 11.5% and EBITDA margin rose 135 bps to 5.3%, with EBITDA up 78% YoY. PAT was INR61 crore (up 66%), but operating cash flow was negative INR46.5 crore in H1 because a Maharashtra government payment of about INR55 crore slipped, lifting NWC days to 64. Management said H1 was ahead of internal plans and reiterated a 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion target, while flagging a one-off INR11.87 crore receivable write-off at a subsidiary.

segments.name: Pharmaceutical distribution
segments.commentary: Core business; organic growth driven by customer base expansion, wallet share gains and new product categories. Management says the company is gaining share ahead of industry growth. Exited certain low-margin accounts, which helped margins.

segments.name: MedTech
segments.commentary: Management says MedTech is at 15%+ of total revenue. Analyst math implies about INR600 crore in H1, which management confirmed. Margin not disclosed; management says margin depends on value-add rather than product type.

segments.name: Government business
segments.commentary: About 2-3% of total revenue (management cited 3%). Long-standing supplier to government agencies and PSUs. Receivables from Maharashtra government contracts were delayed in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance (previously stated): consolidated revenue growth of about 23% excluding new acquisitions, EBITDA margin of 5%, and EBITDA-to-OCF conversion of 50%.
Management says it is 'very comfortable' to beat the revenue and margin guidance but did not give a revised number.
Calendarisation benefit from acquisitions will taper in Q3 and more so in Q4 unless new acquisitions close.
Interest cost of about INR20 crore per quarter should fall once debt repayments on last year's acquisition debt start in Q3.
Management is sticking with the 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion for FY27 and says FY28 guidance will come with Q4 results.
MedTech revenue will exceed INR1,000 crore in FY27, per management.
capex_capacity: No capex plans were discussed on the call.

Acquisitions: no acquisitions closed in H1 FY27. Management is evaluating several opportunities, including large deals in pharma and MedTech, with a minimum size of about INR100 crore and a preference for product-category expansion.
Net debt to EBITDA is capped at 2x by board mandate; surplus cash goes to acquisitions first, with debt repayment as the fallback.
H1 acquisition consideration paid was INR166 crore, all deferred consideration from earlier deals (March balance INR309 crore). Management did not give the remaining balance or its timing.
Call option exists on minority interest; NCI was about 25% of profit before minority interest in Q2 (INR15 crore). No number given for future buyout.
demand_pricing: Scale: over 92,200 retail customers and 2,900+ hospital customers in H1, about 500 districts across 20+ states and UTs, 90,400+ SKUs from 3,200+ manufacturers.
Management says it is gaining share and that the Indian healthcare products market is fragmented and growing at a double-digit pace.

Trade margin cap / NPPA action: 137 molecules notified; these account for about 2% of Entero's portfolio. Management says distributor margin percentages have not changed historically and that any MRP cut mainly hits hospitals and manufacturers.
Industry (IPM) growth reached about 15% in Q2 against a historical 7-10% range, mostly volume-led; management said it does not know the root cause.
A one-off INR11.87 crore receivable default at a subsidiary (pharmacy customer) was fully provided in Other Expenses; post-dated cheques and security are held and legal recovery is being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company upgrading the 23% revenue growth guidance given H1 growth above 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is in a very comfortable position to do better than guidance on growth and margin but gave no new numerical guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the proposed hospital MRP or trade margin caps hurt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no material impact is expected because distributors did not earn the gap; the 11.5% gross margin is all-inclusive, and the molecules notified so far are about 2% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Was the INR12 crore provision a margin drag, and what was the write-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the margin would have been higher without it. It was a customer default at a subsidiary, the full INR11.87 crore is in Other Expenses, and part was already in the opening provision.

qa_highlights.question: Will debt repayment or minority buyouts reduce the minority share over two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers. Operating cash flow will go to acquisitions, minority buyout or organic growth, depending on opportunities; debt is repaid only if no high-ROCE use is found.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 OCF conversion of 50% of EBITDA hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the 50% target for FY27 and said nothing much has changed since the guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach 20% in FY28 without acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will give FY28 numbers at Q4 results. It said organic growth is also a priority and that many organic opportunities are being worked on.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow: H1 OCF was negative INR46.5 crore; the Maharashtra receivable (about INR55 crore) was due in November, and NWC days must come down from 64.
Pricing regulation: NPPA trade margin caps on more molecules or hospital MRP changes could affect top-line prices even if margin percentage holds.
Receivable quality: INR11.87 crore subsidiary default, with recovery uncertain.
Acquisition timing: calendarisation benefit fades in Q3-Q4, so organic growth must carry the rate unless deals close; management said it hopes large deals will close this year.
Leverage and minority interest: board cap of 2x net debt to EBITDA; NCI absorbs about 25% of profit before minority interest.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on H1 growth, margins and the guidance beat, but deliberately vague on specific numbers for FY28, minority buyouts, acquisition size and the subsidiary write-off. Cash-flow timing was framed as a one-off.
key_quotes: What I said in my note, that we are in a very, very comfortable position to better than the guidance that we have provided.
So, any margin, any MRP reduction is not likely to have any impact on our overall margin structure.
Had this money been received on the due date, our H1 operating cash flow would have been positive.
The board, internally, we have this mandate that we will not exceed 2x net debt to EBITDA ratio.

growth.why: Management says it is comfortable beating FY27 guidance of about 23% ex-acquisition revenue growth and 5% EBITDA margin, but gives no revised number; backing is share gains and the fragmented market with no capacity, order or contract figures, and acquisition calendarisation tapers from Q3.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin rose 135 bps to 5.3% and management says FY27 margin will beat the 5% guide, though calendarisation tailwind fades from Q3 and the INR11.87 crore write-off was a drag.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Organic growth of 18.2% (20% like-for-like) and management says it is gaining share in a fragmented market growing at double digits, though calendarisation benefit tapers from Q3.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue grew 35% against FY27 guidance of about 23%, and management says it is 'very comfortable' beating both revenue and margin guidance, though no new number was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated the beat and held the 50% OCF conversion target, but H1 OCF was negative INR46.5 crore and NWC days are 64, so cash-flow risk remains.

rows.label: Maharashtra government receivable (~INR55 crore) collection
rows.why: The payment was due in November and is needed to bring OCF back on track and cut NWC days from 64, though it slipped once already.

rows.label: Acquisitions closing (pharma / MedTech, min ~INR100 crore)
rows.why: No deals closed in H1 and several are under evaluation, with management hoping large deals close this year; calendarisation benefit fades in Q3-Q4 without them.

rows.label: NPPA trade margin caps on 137 molecules
rows.why: The notified molecules are about 2% of portfolio, so direct impact is small, but more molecules or hospital MRP cuts could hit top-line prices.

tone.note: Management was confident on H1 growth, margin and beating FY27 guidance, and on the 50% OCF target, but vague on FY28 numbers, minority buyout, acquisition size and the write-off; analysts pushed on upgrade quantification and cash conversion.
